Nadella first disclosed the milestone on the October 28[1] earnings call: “Over 50 million agents are now in the registry, up over 30% quarter-over-quarter.” Agent 365 launched in May 2026. Gartner forecasts that more than 40% of agentic AI projects will be called off by the end of 2027, partly because of rising costs and unclear value. Danaher said Friday it has partnered with Microsoft to develop an agentic artificial intelligence platform to support its instruments. The partners will create the platform using Microsoft's Azure cloud infrastructure and Foundry system for building and governing AI agents. Danaher plans to start launching agent-enabled instruments this year, with software for its high-content cellular imaging systems among the first products on its roadmap. The partners aim to create AI agents that interpret results and guide instrument control. Areas of focus include building agents that help scientists plan experiments, set up instruments and design methods. Other AI agents will control instrument hardware within defined safety boundaries and under user oversight. The agents will guide execution and troubleshooting, Danaher said. Danaher envisions other Microsoft-enabled agents interpreting data and identifying quality issues in real time, as well as recommending corrective actions and suggesting the next experiments for scientists to review. The system will remain open to agents and digital solutions in multi-vendor laboratories. In preliminary internal testing, novice scientists took up to 83% less time to conduct an experiment on a microscope when working with an AI assistant. The scientists took up to 68% fewer steps to complete the test than their peers working without AI assistance. The AI-assisted novice scientists produced high-quality data and completed the experiments in a time comparable to an expert, Danaher said. Danaher plans to make its MetaXpress Acquire AI Assistant available commercially this year. The company has designed the software to support users of its high-content cellular imaging systems. Danaher plans to launch more agent-enabled instruments next year while continuing to develop the underlying platform. The Microsoft partnership is the latest in a series of Danaher initiatives at the intersection of AI and hardware.
